summary: Jason Berglund, 18, of Alliance, Nebraska — went missing Oct 22, 2014; his car was found two days later at the Colorado Trail/Rolling Creek trailhead off County Road 68 near Bailey. A multi-day four-mile-radius search by the Park County Sheriff's Office, Park County SAR, 35+ volunteers and 7 dog teams found nothing. On 2015-07-09 a hiker found his decaying body ~3 miles up the trail in the Lost Creek Wilderness; PCSAR and the coroner extracted it that afternoon. A rope ligature around his neck was reported as the likely cause of death.
location: Colorado Trail / Rolling Creek trailhead (~3 mi up trail), Lost Creek Wilderness, near Bailey
responding_agency: Park County Sheriff's Office + Park County Search and Rescue
notes: DATE APPROXIMATE: row recorded at the Oct-2014 missing/search date (car seen at the Bailey trailhead 2014-10-24; exact search days in late Oct 2014 unreported), following the Stehling-row convention; body found and extracted 2015-07-09. Missing since 2014-10-22 (left University of Nebraska–Kearney in a 2000 Dodge Intrepid); ATM sighting in downtown Denver 2014-10-23. Identified via dental records; wake July 17, 2015 in Alliance, NE. Dedupe: no Berglund/Rolling Creek tokens in DB; Park 2014-09–12 window rows (id 220 Elevenmile Canyon, id 1951 Wellington Lake) are distinct incidents. SARDOC June 2-4 2015 mission report: human remains (a scapula, complete arm and hand) found by nearby school personnel near Rolling Creek/CR 68 and the Colorado Trail, Park County; a SARDOC dog found a glove ~150 ft away plus a clear drag mark below and above the remains; searched the area for further remains, found nothing. The report notes the remains are believed tied to the October 2014 search for a missing 19-year-old from Nebraska in the same area — consistent with Berglund (whose dental-ID'd body was found July 9, 2015 ~3 mi up the trail). Logged as probable-same; kept as one row, no separate insert. SARDOC Q4-2014 public mission summaries: SARDOC dog-team assists on 2014-10-30, 10/31, 11/1, 11/2, 11/5 and 11/10 in the multi-agency search; search to continue in spring.
